summary: All 23 claimed orbits (16 fully reviewed, 7 added later and checked with the same independent integrator) are genuine collisionless periodic orbits with the stated minimal period and words. They carry 9 new words, (Ba)^n(bA)^n for n = 4..12 (rungs k = 3..11). Novelty was checked only against the Li-Liao catalogues and papers available locally; no wider literature search was possible, and the Sofia group's equal-mass databases could not be opened.

cards.title: Periodic
cards.text: An independent code (SciPy DOP853 at 10⁻¹³, and implicit Radau IIA for the first 16) closes every orbit to between 10⁻¹¹ and 8×10⁻⁹. For 22 of the 23 the residual shrinks as the tolerance tightens. Rung 3 at m₃ = 0.5 sits on a 5×10⁻¹⁰ floor that the reviewer's Newton step removes by moving T by 2×10⁻¹⁰. For the first 16, the reviewer's Newton step moves the velocities by at most 10⁻¹². Each stated period is the shortest one, and no orbit comes closer than 0.025 to a collision.

cards.title: Named correctly
cards.text: For the first 16 orbits, a second topology code, written from scratch with two different ways of reading the crossings, reproduces every word exactly, under both labelling conventions that match the published words of known orbits. Every crossing of the equator is clean, far from the collision points. The 7 rungs added later carry the same words, computed by our own code.

cards.title: Not in the catalogues
cards.text: None of the rung words for k = 3 to 11 matches any of the 2,360 words in the Li & Liao catalogues under any physical symmetry (rotation, time reversal, mirror image, swapping the equal stars). At m₃ = 0.5 and 0.75 no catalogued orbit has the same word. The three catalogued m₃ = 0.5 orbits within 1% in scale-free period have different words and start from velocities 0.09 to 0.38 away. These rungs lie inside the window the 2018 survey searched.

cards.title: Anchored to known orbits
cards.text: Following rung 1 from m₃ = 0.25 upward lands on Li, Jing & Liao's I.A i.c. 2 at m₃ = 0.75 (velocities to every published digit, period to one unit in the tenth decimal) and on Li & Liao's equal-mass I.A i.c. 3 (velocities within 6×10⁻¹¹, period within 2.4×10⁻⁹). The published equal-mass values close only to about 5×10⁻⁷ and Newton-refine onto our orbit. This checks the search, the continuation and the slice conventions end to end.

cards.title: Not checked
cards.text: No literature search beyond the local Li & Liao catalogues and papers was possible here. Unread sources include the Sofia group's equal-mass databases (Hristov, Hristova and coauthors, 2022–2026; their 2024 Euler-configuration set has 6,333 solutions), the Šuvakov–Dmitrašinović gallery, and Dmitrašinović et al. (2018). If the higher rungs reach m₃ = 1, some of these words may already be listed there.

cards.title: Not new
cards.text: Periods that grow in step with word length are the topological dependence of Kepler's third law (Dmitrašinović & Šuvakov 2015). Ladders of words are known too, for example (BA)ⁿ(ba)ⁿ. What is new here is these rungs and orbits, not the pattern.
